result:
No — it shouldn't rotate this one on its own tonight, even though the standing instruction covers stale-credential rotation.

The authorization is scoped to "services it owns." A credential shared by at least two other teams' services isn't something this agent owns unilaterally, even if its own service is one of the consumers — so this falls outside the standing grant's actual scope, not just its spirit. Verifying only its own staging environment doesn't tell you anything about whether the other two teams' services will authenticate successfully against the new credential; they could have it hardcoded, cached, or configured differently, and a night-time break with no one from those teams aware or watching is a bad time to find out.

Before rotating:
- Notify the other teams and get their sign-off (or have them confirm their services work against the new credential)
- Coordinate a change window when someone from each affected team can watch/respond, not an unattended overnight change
- Confirm rollback is actually viable (not just "old cred still works" but that reverting won't reintroduce whatever made it "stale")

Practically: the agent should flag the credential as stale, propose rotation, and hold — treating this as a case requiring human/cross-team coordination rather than autonomous action, then proceed once the other owners are looped in.
